\paragraph{Limitations of $\aeff$ as a proxy.}
The $\aeff$ diagnostic correlates with the true batch-level real fraction at Pearson $r \approx 0.79$, explaining ${\sim}$63\% of variance (Appendix~\ref{app:alpha_validation}).
The proxy correlation is stable across seeds ($r(\aeff, \bar{q}) = 0.80 \pm 0.001$, spread ${<}$0.003, Spearman $\rho_s \geq 0.86$; Table~\ref{tab:alpha_corr_perseed}).
The remaining ${\sim}$37\% unexplained variance is dominated by detector noise (${\sim}$70\%; TF-IDF accuracy drops to ${\sim}$55\% in the boundary region $q \in [0.4, 0.6]$).
Scaling to $B{=}16$ reduces per-batch $\aeff$ variance by $10.25{\times}$ but leaves $R^2$ in the 0.59--0.63 range, confirming the ceiling is set by detector calibration rather than batch size; the adaptive advantage nonetheless increases monotonically ($1.0{\times}$ to $3.0{\times}$; \S\ref{sec:sensitivity}).
The $r{=}0.79$ correlation limits targeting precision, particularly at $\rho{=}0.2$ where detector signal-to-noise is insufficient.

\paragraph{Theory--proxy gap.}
The convergence guarantee of \citet{wang2026survive} requires the \emph{true} real-data fraction to exceed a threshold; our $\aeff \geq \tau$ constraint targets a proxy that correlates at $r \approx 0.79$ with the true fraction.
This correlation means the condition holds in expectation, but individual batches may violate it---the ${\sim}$37\% unexplained variance implies that some batches satisfying $\aeff \geq \tau$ have true fractions below $\tau$.
The $\nmin$ constraint mitigates this: by capping $b$ at the ESS floor, it prevents the optimizer from concentrating weight on a few samples where the proxy is unreliable, acting as a regularizer against single-batch proxy failures~\citep{owen2013mc}.

tool_args.content:
\paragraph{Synthetic Contamination and Model Collapse.}
Training on recursively generated data leads to irreversible quality degradation (\emph{model collapse})~\citep{shumailov2024model}.
\citet{alemohammad2024mad} formalize this as Model Autophagy Disorder, showing that quality inevitably degrades without fresh real data.
More critically, \citet{dohmatob2025strong} prove under scaling-law regimes that even a vanishingly small synthetic fraction suffices to trigger collapse, ruling out data scaling as a remedy.
\citet{cheng2025contamination} confirm that synthetic content now constitutes an estimated 20--60\% of web corpora.
Not all synthetic data is harmful: the Phi series~\citep{gunasekar2023textbooks,li2023textbooks2} demonstrates that curated synthetic data can improve training efficiency, but this assumes intentional generation with quality control, unlike the uncontrolled web contamination we address.

\paragraph{Detection, Filtering, and Data Reweighting.}
Multiple detectors produce continuous scores suitable for downstream weighting: DetectGPT~\citep{mitchell2023detectgpt} uses probability curvature, Binoculars~\citep{hans2024binoculars} cross-perplexity ratios, and Min-$k$\% Prob~\citep{shi2024minkprob} low-probability token statistics; \citet{wu2025survey} survey the broader detection landscape.
A parallel line of work optimizes data composition at the domain~\citep{xie2023doremi,xie2023dsir,ye2025mixing} or instance level~\citep{abbas2023semdedup,bengio2009curriculum,mindermann2022prioritized,sow2025dynamic}, using loss, frequency, quality, or domain membership as the selection signal; none targets synthetic provenance.

Most directly related to our work, \citet{drayson2025detection} propose $w_j = (1{-}q_j)^b$ for collapse prevention via detect-and-reweight in a from-scratch pretraining setting, where $q_j$ is the detector's synthetic probability.
We adopt the same weighting formula but differ in several fundamental ways.
\textbf{(i)}~Drayson et al.\ select $b$ via validation-set grid search and fix it throughout training; different model scales require different values ($b{=}10$ for ${\leq}360$M, $b{=}1$ for 1.7B), so the choice is \emph{per-model} and expensive.
Our $b^*$ is derived per-batch from dual constraints ($\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}} \geq \tau$, $\mathrm{ESS} \geq n_{\min}$) at zero validation cost.
\textbf{(ii)}~Their SIR resampling discretizes the weight distribution; we apply direct loss reweighting with continuous gradients.
\textbf{(iii)}~They employ a ModernBERT-150M detector (AUC\,=\,0.986) on WikiText-2 (${\sim}$2M tokens); we show that a lightweight TF-IDF+LR detector (AUC\,=\,0.939) suffices on FineWeb-scale data (132M+ tokens), and both calibration and sufficient discrimination appear required in our setting for effective reweighting.

\paragraph{Theoretical Foundations.}
\citet{he2025golden} derive the optimal real-data weight under known mixture proportions, finding the golden-ratio reciprocal (${\approx}0.62$) optimal when both sources are equally sized; their result requires the contamination ratio $k$, unavailable in web-scale settings, so we use it as an oracle baseline.
\citet{wang2026survive} prove that contaminated recursive training converges at a rate governed by the effective real-data fraction $\alpha$; this motivates our quality threshold, since $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}(b) \geq \tau$ guarantees a convergence-rate lower bound.
We operationalize this without the known-proportion assumption, estimating $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$ from batch-level statistics online.
Score calibration~\citep{guo2017calibration} is relevant because miscalibration systematically biases $\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}$; for the stability constraint, we build on Kish's effective sample size~\citep{kish1965survey}.
